sentence: कल उसने गरम रोटी खाई।
english: Yesterday she (or he) ate a hot roti.
harm: The learner is not told that ने marks the doer, and that खाई is feminine because it agrees with रोटी and not with the person who ate.

sentence: मैंने कल एक नई किताब पढ़ी।
english: I read a new book yesterday.
harm: The learner is told पढ़ी agrees with "I" and is shown a wrong rule; it is feminine because of किताब, whoever the speaker is.

sentence: लड़की ने अपनी माँ को चिट्ठी लिखी।
english: The girl wrote a letter to her mother.
harm: The learner is told लिखी agrees with the mother, who takes को, when it agrees with the letter.
notes: को marks the indirect object here (the mother), so it does not block agreement with चिट्ठी.

sentence: माँ ने त्योहार पर दो मिठाइयाँ बनाईं।
english: Mother made two sweets for the festival.
harm: The learner is told बनाईं is singular like "mother", and misses that a plural object makes the verb plural.

sentence: उसने बच्चे को स्कूल में देखा।
english: He (or she) saw the child at school.
harm: The learner is not told that when the object has को the verb stays masculine singular and does not agree with it.

sentence: मैंने सीता को कल बाज़ार में बुलाया।
english: I called Sita to the market yesterday.
harm: The learner is told the verb should be feminine (बुलाई) because Sita is a woman, when the verb stays masculine singular with a को object.

sentence: हमने बाग़ से ताज़े फल तोड़े।
english: We picked fresh fruit from the garden.
harm: The learner is told तोड़े is an adjective or a noun and misses the plural verb that agrees with फल.
notes: फल is a masculine noun whose plural looks like its singular; the plural verb तोड़े shows the object is plural here.

sentence: सीता बाज़ार से सब्ज़ियाँ लाई।
english: Sita brought vegetables from the market.
harm: The learner is told a ने is missing, or that लाई should agree with the plural vegetables (लाईं); लाना takes no ने and agrees with the doer.
notes: Reviewer: please confirm that लाना takes no ने in standard Hindi (the usual textbook position); I am fairly sure but it is a point of usage.

sentence: मैं अपनी चाबी घर पर भूल गई।
english: I forgot my key at home.
harm: The learner is told "went" and "forgot" are two separate actions, and that a ने is missing; भूलना takes no ने and भूल गई is one verb.
notes: The speaker is taken to be a woman; the sentence is also a compound verb.

sentence: वह धीमी आवाज़ में कुछ बोली।
english: She said something in a low voice.
harm: The learner is told बोली is an adjective ("spoken", a language) or that a ने is missing; बोलना takes no ने and agrees with the doer.
notes: Reviewer: बोलना can also take ने in some usage (उसने कुछ बोला); please say which is the unmarked form for a learner.

sentence: तुमने मुझसे यह बात क्यों नहीं कही?
english: Why did you not tell me this?
harm: The learner is told कही agrees with "you" and is not shown that it follows बात.

sentence: उन्होंने पूरा खाना खा लिया।
english: They ate up the whole meal.
harm: The learner is not told that उन्होंने is "they" plus ने written as one word, and that the verb agrees with खाना.
notes: The split of उन्होंने is written उन्हों + ने (as spelled); please say if you prefer another cut. The same sentence is also a compound verb खा लेना. Lemma convention to confirm: PLAN12 says a pronoun's lemma is its direct form; I expect the dictionary headword वह for उन्होंने, उन, उन्हें and वे (and यह for ये, इन).

sentence: बहन ने भाई को एक लंबी चिट्ठी भेजी।
english: The sister sent her brother a long letter.
harm: The learner is told भेजी agrees with the brother, when it agrees with the letter because the object has no को.

sentence: किसने यह चित्र बनाया?
english: Who made this picture?
harm: The learner is told किसने is a single unknown word and does not see that "who" is in the ergative.
notes: Reviewer: is चित्र masculine? I believe yes (चित्र बनाया).

sentence: मुझे सुबह से बहुत भूख लगी है।
english: I have been very hungry since morning.
harm: The learner is told "I felt hunger" has "I" as its subject, and misses that लगी agrees with भूख.

sentence: उसे अभी ठंडा पानी चाहिए।
english: He (or she) needs cold water right now.
harm: The learner is told उसे is the object and that चाहिए has a different subject, instead of "he needs".

sentence: मुझे यह पुराना गाना बहुत पसंद है।
english: I like this old song a lot.
harm: The learner is told the song "likes" something or that "I" is the object, when मुझे is the one who likes.

sentence: तुम्हें अंग्रेज़ी अच्छी तरह आती है।
english: You know English well.
harm: The learner is told आती means "comes" literally and misses that आना here means "to know (a skill)", agreeing with अंग्रेज़ी.

sentence: शिक्षक ने छात्रों को नई किताबें दीं।
english: The teacher gave the students new books.
harm: The learner is told the students are what was given, when को marks the receiver and the books are the thing given.

sentence: मैं इस लड़के को अच्छी तरह जानता हूँ।
english: I know this boy well.
harm: The learner is not told that को marks a particular, known person as the object.

sentence: उन्हें नई गाड़ी बहुत पसंद आई।
english: They liked the new car a lot.
harm: The learner is told आई means "came" and that the car came to them, and misses पसंद आना as one unit meaning "to be liked".
notes: Lemma convention to confirm: I expect वह for उन्हें (dictionary headword); the engine may follow PLAN12's "direct form" and give वे.

sentence: उसे यह सुनकर बहुत गुस्सा आया।
english: He (or she) got very angry on hearing this.
harm: The learner is told anger "came" as a separate event and misses that गुस्सा आना is one expression meaning "to become angry".

sentence: मुझे कल सुबह जल्दी उठना है।
english: I have to get up early tomorrow morning.
harm: The learner is told उठना है means "is getting up" and misses that infinitive plus है with को means "must".

sentence: बच्चों को मीठा दूध पसंद है।
english: The children like sweet milk.
harm: The learner is told the children are the object and that the milk is the one who likes.

sentence: वह एक अच्छा लड़का है।
english: He is a good boy.
harm: The learner is not shown that अच्छा ends in -ा because लड़का is masculine singular.

sentence: हमारे गाँव में एक बड़ी नदी है।
english: There is a big river in our village.
harm: The learner is told बड़ी is a different word from बड़ा, instead of the feminine form agreeing with नदी.

sentence: मेरे भाई का घर बहुत बड़ा है।
english: My brother's house is very big.
harm: The learner is told का agrees with the brother (the owner) and not with the house.

sentence: मेरे भाई की किताब मेज़ पर है।
english: My brother's book is on the table.
harm: The learner is told की is the verb "did" or that it agrees with the brother, when it is feminine because of किताब.

sentence: उसके बच्चों के कपड़े नए हैं।
english: His children's clothes are new.
harm: The learner is told के agrees with the children, when it agrees with कपड़े.

sentence: इन किताबों की क़ीमत बहुत ज़्यादा है।
english: The price of these books is very high.
harm: The learner is told की agrees with किताबों (the owner), when it is feminine because of क़ीमत.

sentence: लड़कियाँ मैदान में दौड़ रही हैं।
english: The girls are running in the field.
harm: The learner is told रही is a verb of staying and misses that the progressive agrees with the girls.

sentence: मेरी बहन रोज़ सुबह दौड़ती है।
english: My sister runs every morning.
harm: The learner is told the verb is masculine, or is not shown that the -ती ending agrees with the sister.

sentence: सब लड़के बाहर खेल रहे थे।
english: All the boys were playing outside.
harm: The learner is told रहे means "stayed" and that the boys were doing something else.

sentence: माँ ने सुबह ताज़ी सब्ज़ियाँ काटीं।
english: Mother cut fresh vegetables in the morning.
harm: The learner is told the verb is singular like "mother" and that ताज़ी is a noun.

sentence: उसने नीली और सुंदर साड़ी पहनी।
english: She wore a blue and beautiful sari.
harm: The learner is told सुंदर is wrong because it did not change like नीली, but adjectives that do not end in -ा never change.

sentence: कमरे की सारी खिड़कियाँ खुली थीं।
english: All the windows of the room were open.
harm: The learner is told थीं is a different word from था or that the verb agrees with the room.
notes: In "कमरे की खिड़कियाँ" की agrees with खिड़कियाँ and कमरे is oblique singular before it.

sentence: मैंने लड़के को घर पर बुलाया।
english: I called the boy to the house.
harm: The learner is told लड़के is plural "boys" and that the boys were called, when it is the singular before को.

sentence: आज सारे लड़के स्कूल नहीं गए।
english: Today all the boys did not go to school.
harm: The learner is told लड़के is the singular before a postposition, when it is the plural "boys" with no postposition after it.

sentence: तीन कमरे अभी खाली हैं।
english: Three rooms are empty at the moment.
harm: The learner is told कमरे is the oblique singular, when it is plural: a -े noun with no postposition after it is plural.

sentence: मैंने कमरे में दो कुर्सियाँ रखीं।
english: I put two chairs in the room.
harm: The learner is told there are several rooms, when कमरे is singular here because में follows it.

sentence: मैं रोज़ लड़कों के साथ क्रिकेट खेलता हूँ।
english: I play cricket with the boys every day.
harm: The learner is not shown that -ों is the plural form used before a postposition.

sentence: लड़कियों की किताबें मेज़ पर रखी हैं।
english: The girls' books are lying on the table.
harm: The learner is told लड़कियों is the subject, when it is the oblique plural before की.
notes: The Case=Dir expectation on किताबें follows PLAN12 (nouns carry Dir / Obl / Voc); it is the Obl on लड़कियों that matters for the learner.

sentence: चाचा ने घोड़े को ताज़ी घास दी।
english: Uncle gave the horse some fresh grass.
harm: The learner is told several horses were fed, when घोड़े is singular because को follows.

sentence: सड़क पर तीन घोड़े खड़े थे।
english: Three horses were standing on the road.
harm: The learner is told घोड़े is the oblique singular and not the plural subject of थे.

sentence: वे दोस्तों के साथ बाज़ार गए।
english: They went to the market with friends.
harm: The learner is told दोस्तों is an unknown word or a singular, when -ों marks the plural before के साथ.

sentence: बच्चो, अब चुपचाप बैठ जाओ।
english: Children, now sit down quietly.
harm: The learner is told बच्चो is a misspelling of बच्चों, when it is the vocative plural used to call out.

sentence: तुम छोटे बच्चे को दूध दो।
english: Give milk to the small child.
harm: The learner is told the children are plural, when the adjective and the noun both take -े because को follows a singular.

sentence: वे खेलने के लिए बाहर गए।
english: They went outside to play.
harm: The learner is told खेलने is a different verb form or a command, and misses that the infinitive ends in -ने before के लिए.

sentence: ये मेरे पुराने दोस्त हैं।
english: These are my old friends.
harm: The learner is told ये is "he" or a particle, and not "these" (the plural of यह).
notes: Lemma convention to confirm: I expect यह (the dictionary headword) for ये; PLAN12 says "direct form", which could also be read as ये itself.

sentence: वे कल सुबह दिल्ली से आए।
english: They came from Delhi yesterday morning.
harm: The learner is told वे is a singular "he", when it is "they" (or a respected "he").
notes: Lemma convention to confirm: I expect वह (the dictionary headword) for वे; the engine may keep वे as its own lemma.

sentence: इस घर में अब कोई नहीं रहता।
english: Nobody lives in this house any more.
harm: The learner is told इस is a different word from यह, when it is the oblique form used before में.

sentence: उन लोगों ने मुझे घर बुलाया।
english: Those people invited me home.
harm: The learner is told उन is a different word from वे, when it is the plural oblique form before लोगों.
notes: Lemma convention to confirm: I expect वह for उन; the engine may give वे.

sentence: मुझ पर भरोसा रखो।
english: Trust me.
harm: The learner is told मुझ is an unknown word, when it is the form of "I" used before a postposition.

sentence: मुझे तुझसे कुछ ज़रूरी बात कहनी है।
english: I have something important to tell you.
harm: The learner is not told that तुझसे is the very intimate तू plus से and that it can sound rude with a stranger.

sentence: रात को किसी ने दरवाज़ा खटखटाया।
english: Someone knocked on the door in the night.
harm: The learner is told किसी means "whose" or "who", when here it means "someone".
notes: Unsure of the lemma: कोई (indefinite) or कौन; I believe कोई for this meaning. Please decide.

sentence: जिन लोगों से मैं मिला, वे सब अच्छे थे।
english: The people I met were all nice.
harm: The learner is told जिन is a question word, when it is the relative "whom" paired with वे.

sentence: आप आजकल कहाँ रहते हैं?
english: Where do you live these days?
harm: The learner is not told that आप is the respectful "you" and takes plural verbs.

sentence: तुम कल कितने बजे आओगे?
english: At what time will you come tomorrow?
harm: The learner is not told that तुम is the familiar "you", between आप and तू.

sentence: तू मेरा सबसे अच्छा दोस्त है।
english: You are my best friend.
harm: The learner is told तू is the usual "you", when it is intimate or rude depending on who speaks.

sentence: वह अपने घर जा रहा है।
english: He is going to his own house.
harm: The learner is told अपने means "his" like उसके, and misses that it points back to the subject.

sentence: बच्चा रात को जल्दी सो गया।
english: The child fell asleep early in the night.
harm: The learner is told the child "slept" and then "went", when सो गया is one compound verb meaning "fell asleep".

sentence: उसने पूरा खाना खा लिया।
english: He (or she) ate the whole meal up.
harm: The learner is told लिया means "took" and misses that खा लिया is "ate it up", a finished action.

sentence: मैंने उसे सब कुछ बता दिया।
english: I told him (or her) everything.
harm: The learner is told दिया means "gave" and that something was given, when बता दिया is "told it all".

sentence: अचानक ज़ोर से बारिश होने लगी।
english: Suddenly it began to rain hard.
harm: The learner is told लगी means "felt" or "was attached" and misses that होने लगी is "began to happen".
notes: Strictly this is an infinitive plus लगना rather than a stem compound; I list it because learners meet it as a unit. Reviewer: keep or move to auxiliary-chain?

sentence: छोटा बच्चा सीढ़ियों पर गिर पड़ा।
english: The little child fell down on the stairs.
harm: The learner is told पड़ा means "lay" and that the child fell and then lay, when गिर पड़ा is one sudden fall.

sentence: गुस्से में उसने गिलास तोड़ डाला।
english: In anger he (or she) smashed the glass.
harm: The learner is told डाला means "put" and misses the sense of a violent, final action.

sentence: थका हुआ आदमी कुर्सी पर बैठ गया।
english: The tired man sat down on the chair.
harm: The learner is told the man sat and then went away, when बैठ गया is "sat down".

sentence: सबकी बातें सुनकर वह अचानक बोल उठा।
english: Hearing everyone, he suddenly spoke up.
harm: The learner is told उठा means "got up" and misses that बोल उठा is "burst out speaking".

sentence: तुम यह चिट्ठी ध्यान से पढ़ लो।
english: Read this letter carefully (for yourself).
harm: The learner is told लो means "take" and that the letter is to be taken, when पढ़ लो is "read it through".

sentence: उसने सारी बातें काग़ज़ पर लिख डालीं।
english: He (or she) wrote all the things down on paper.
harm: The learner is told डालीं is a separate verb "put" and misses the feminine plural agreement with बातें.

sentence: किसी ने चुपचाप दरवाज़ा खोल दिया।
english: Someone quietly opened the door.
harm: The learner is told दिया means "gave" and that a door was given to someone, when खोल दिया is "opened it".

sentence: सुबह होते ही वह घर से निकल पड़ा।
english: As soon as it was morning he set out from home.
harm: The learner is told पड़ा means "lay" and misses that निकल पड़ा is "set out".

sentence: वह बाज़ार से किताब लेकर आया।
english: He came from the market carrying a book.
harm: The learner is told लेकर आया is the compound "brought", when it is two actions joined by कर: "having taken (it), came".
notes: Look-alike of cv-014. The -कर form is a conjunctive participle, not a compound; the difference in meaning is small, the grammar is not.

sentence: वह बाज़ार से किताब ले आया।
english: He brought a book from the market.
harm: The learner is told ले and आया are two separate actions, when ले आया is one compound verb "brought".
notes: Reviewer: is ले आना a compound verb (stem + आना) for your purposes? I believe so.

sentence: उसने दरवाज़ा खोलकर बाहर देखा।
english: Having opened the door, he (or she) looked outside.
harm: The learner is told खोलकर देखा is one compound verb, when these are two independent actions joined by कर.

sentence: वह दिन भर खेत में बहुत काम करता है।
english: He works a great deal in the field all day.
harm: The learner is told "does" and "work" separately and does not see that काम करना is the verb "to work".

sentence: मुझे अपना बचपन अक्सर याद आता है।
english: I often remember my childhood.
harm: The learner is told "memory comes" word for word and misses that याद आना is one expression, "to be reminded, to recall".

sentence: नाटक आज शाम सात बजे शुरू होगा।
english: The play will begin at seven this evening.
harm: The learner is told होगा is a separate future "will be" and misses शुरू होना as "to begin".

sentence: क्या तुम कल मेरी थोड़ी मदद कर सकते हो?
english: Could you help me a little tomorrow?
harm: The learner is told मदद and कर सकते are unrelated words and that "can do" is the point, when मदद करना ("to help") is the unit.
notes: The object-adjective मेरी थोड़ी stands between मदद and कर; the unit should still be found.

sentence: हमने नई पढ़ाई सोमवार से शुरू की।
english: We started the new course of study on Monday.
harm: The learner is told की is "of" (का) here, when it is the feminine past of करना agreeing with पढ़ाई.

sentence: हम बस का इंतज़ार कर रहे हैं।
english: We are waiting for the bus.
harm: The learner is told the bus is "of" something and that the verb is "stay", and misses इंतज़ार करना as "to wait".

sentence: मैं अपने दोस्त पर पूरा भरोसा करता हूँ।
english: I trust my friend completely.
harm: The learner is not told that भरोसा करना is one expression "to trust" and that the person trusted takes पर.

sentence: उसे पहली ही नज़र में उससे प्यार हो गया।
english: He (or she) fell in love with him (or her) at first sight.
harm: The learner is told "love became" or "went" word for word, and misses that प्यार होना (with से) means "to fall in love".

sentence: तुम इस सवाल का जवाब दो।
english: Answer this question.
harm: The learner is told "give an answer" word for word and misses that जवाब देना is the verb "to answer".

sentence: आप इसकी चिंता मत कीजिए।
english: Please do not worry about it.
harm: The learner is told कीजिए is a stand-alone "do" and misses that चिंता करना is "to worry".

sentence: उसने दोपहर में दो घंटे आराम किया।
english: He (or she) rested for two hours in the afternoon.
harm: The learner is told किया is "did" and misses that आराम करना is "to rest".

sentence: जाते समय तुम दरवाज़ा बंद कर देना।
english: When you leave, close the door.
harm: The learner is told बंद is a noun and misses that बंद करना ("to close, to shut") is the unit, with देना added on top.
notes: This is also a compound verb (कर देना) on top of the complex predicate; the unit I mean is बंद करना.

sentence: माँ बच्चे को खाना खिलाती है।
english: Mother feeds the child.
harm: The learner is told खिलाती is a form of खाना "to eat" and that the mother eats, when the causative means "to feed".

sentence: शिक्षक छात्रों को हिंदी पढ़ाते हैं।
english: The teacher teaches the students Hindi.
harm: The learner is told पढ़ाते means "read" and that the teacher is reading, when the causative means "teach".

sentence: उसने मुझसे यह काम करवाया।
english: He (or she) had me do this work.
harm: The learner is told "he did the work", and misses that करवाना means getting someone else (मुझसे) to do it.

sentence: मैंने दर्ज़ी से अपने कपड़े सिलवाए।
english: I had my clothes sewn by a tailor.
harm: The learner is told the speaker sewed the clothes himself, when the -वा causative says the tailor did it.

sentence: माँ बच्चे को सुला रही है।
english: Mother is putting the child to sleep.
harm: The learner is told the mother is sleeping, when सुलाना is "to put to sleep".
notes: सुला is the stem; its lemma is सुलाना (causative of सोना).

sentence: वह रोज़ अपने मज़ाक से मुझे हँसाता है।
english: He makes me laugh every day with his jokes.
harm: The learner is told हँसाता is "laughs" and that he is the one laughing, when it means "makes (me) laugh".

sentence: पिताजी ने नौकर से गाड़ी धुलवाई।
english: Father had the servant wash the car.
harm: The learner is told father washed the car, and misses that the servant does it and that the verb agrees with गाड़ी.

sentence: उसने नौकर से कमरा साफ़ कराया।
english: He (or she) had the servant clean the room.
harm: The learner is told the subject cleaned the room, when कराना (the causative of करना) says someone else did it.
notes: The unit pattern is written with the causative lemma कराना, not करना, because the causative is the lemma of the verb actually present.

sentence: मुझे मत रुलाओ, मैं पहले ही दुखी हूँ।
english: Do not make me cry; I am unhappy already.
harm: The learner is told रुलाओ is "cry" (रोओ), when it is "make cry".

sentence: यहाँ ज़्यादातर हिंदी बोली जाती है।
english: Hindi is mostly spoken here.
harm: The learner is told Hindi "goes" or that someone "speaks and goes", when बोली जाती है is a passive: "is spoken".

sentence: कल रात दुकान का ताला तोड़ा गया।
english: The lock of the shop was broken last night.
harm: The learner is told तोड़ा गया is a compound "broke and went", when it is a passive: "was broken".

sentence: इस किताब में सौ कहानियाँ लिखी गई हैं।
english: A hundred stories have been written in this book.
harm: The learner is told the stories "went" somewhere, when लिखी गई हैं is a passive: "have been written".

sentence: शहर में नई सड़क बनाई जा रही है।
english: A new road is being built in the city.
harm: The learner is told जा रही है is "is going" and the road is walking, when it is the progressive passive "is being built".

sentence: यह पत्र कल डाक से भेजा जाएगा।
english: This letter will be sent by post tomorrow.
harm: The learner is told जाएगा means "will go" and that the letter will travel, when it forms the passive "will be sent".

sentence: वह अचानक कमरे से चला गया।
english: He suddenly left the room.
harm: The learner is told चला गया is a passive "was walked", when it is the compound "went away" with an active subject.
notes: The contrast with the passive items: चला is the participle of चलना and गया adds "away".

sentence: यह कपड़ा मशीन में धोया जाता है।
english: This cloth is washed in a machine.
harm: The learner is told the cloth "goes" and washes something, when धोया जाता है is the passive "is washed".

sentence: जो विद्यार्थी रोज़ पढ़ता है, वह परीक्षा में सफल होता है।
english: The student who studies every day succeeds in the exam.
harm: The learner is told जो means "what?" and does not see that the जो-clause is picked up by वह.

sentence: जब बारिश होती है, तब हम घर में रहते हैं।
english: When it rains, we stay at home.
harm: The learner is told जब and तब are unrelated words ("when" and "then"), not a matching pair.

sentence: जहाँ तुम जाओगे, वहाँ मैं भी जाऊँगा।
english: Where you go, I will go too.
harm: The learner is not shown that जहाँ opens a clause which वहाँ answers.

sentence: जैसा काम करोगे, वैसा फल पाओगे।
english: As you work, so you will be rewarded.
harm: The learner is told जैसा and वैसा are plain adjectives with no link to each other.

sentence: जितना तुम सोचते हो, काम उतना मुश्किल नहीं है।
english: The work is not as hard as you think.
harm: The learner is not shown that जितना and उतना measure one amount against another.

sentence: जिसने यह चित्र बनाया है, वह मेरी बहन है।
english: The one who made this picture is my sister.
harm: The learner is told जिसने is the question "who?" when it is the relative "the one who", answered by वह.

sentence: जब मैं घर पहुँचा, वह सो रहा था।
english: When I reached home, he was asleep.
harm: The learner is told जब is only a question word, when it opens a clause even without तब after it.
notes: तब is left out, as it often is; the pair is still a jab-tab sentence.

sentence: जो किताब मैंने कल ली थी, वह बहुत अच्छी है।
english: The book that I took yesterday is very good.
harm: The learner is told जो किताब is a question and that वह begins a new statement, not an answer to the relative clause.

sentence: पिताजी आज देर से घर आए।
english: Father came home late today.
harm: The learner is told आए means there is more than one father, when the plural is used out of respect for one person.

sentence: दादाजी सुबह बाग़ में टहल रहे हैं।
english: Grandfather is strolling in the garden in the morning.
harm: The learner is told रहे हैं is a plural subject, when it shows respect for one grandfather.

sentence: आप यहाँ आराम से बैठिए।
english: Please sit down here comfortably.
harm: The learner is not told that -इए is the polite command used with आप, and may use बैठ or बैठो to a stranger.

sentence: कृपया मुझे सच बताइए।
english: Please tell me the truth.
harm: The learner is told बताइए is a past or a plural form, when it is the polite command.

sentence: आप यह फ़ॉर्म भर दीजिए।
english: Please fill in this form.
harm: The learner is told दीजिए means "please give" and misses भर दीजिए as the polite "fill it in".

sentence: शर्मा जी कल दिल्ली जा रहे हैं।
english: Mr Sharma is going to Delhi tomorrow.
harm: The learner is told जी is a name or a verb, and that the plural रहे हैं means a group.
notes: Unsure of part of speech and lemma of the respect marker जी here; please say what a learner should be shown.

sentence: आप आज कैसे हैं?
english: How are you today?
harm: The learner is told हैं is "they are" and that आप means a group, when आप takes हैं even for one person.

sentence: आप वहाँ मत जाइए।
english: Please do not go there.
harm: The learner is not told that मत with -इए is the polite "please don't".

sentence: मेरी माँ आज बाहर गई हैं।
english: My mother has gone out today.
harm: The learner is told हैं means there are several mothers, when the plural verb shows respect.

sentence: वह रोज़ सुबह एक गिलास दूध पीता है।
english: He drinks a glass of milk every morning.
harm: The learner is told पीता है is a one-time event, when -ता है says it happens regularly.

sentence: बचपन में हम रोज़ नदी पर खेलते थे।
english: In childhood we used to play on the river every day.
harm: The learner is told खेलते थे is a single event in the past, when it says it used to happen.

sentence: वह इस समय खाना खा रहा है।
english: He is eating at the moment.
harm: The learner is told रहा means "stayed" and that the sentence says he has stayed eating, when रहा is the auxiliary marking that the action is in progress.

sentence: माँ रसोई में खाना बना रही थी।
english: Mother was cooking in the kitchen.
harm: The learner is told रही is the verb "to stay" and that mother stayed in the kitchen, and misses that the cooking was going on.

sentence: वह दो साल तक दिल्ली में रहा।
english: He lived in Delhi for two years.
harm: The learner is told रहा is a progressive auxiliary when here it is the main verb "stayed, lived".
notes: The mirror of aux-003: the same form रहा, read as a full verb because nothing precedes it.

sentence: वह अभी घर पहुँचा है।
english: He has just reached home.
harm: The learner is told पहुँचा है is a simple past, when -ा है says the result still holds now.

sentence: जब मैं पहुँचा, वह जा चुका था।
english: When I arrived, he had already gone.
harm: The learner is told चुका is a stand-alone word or a noun, and misses that चुकना marks the action as already finished.

sentence: कल हम सब बाज़ार जाएँगे।
english: Tomorrow we will all go to the market.
harm: The learner is told जाएँगे is a form of the present, and does not see the -ए- subjunctive stem plus -गे.

sentence: शायद वह कल सुबह आए।
english: Perhaps he will come tomorrow morning.
harm: The learner is told आए is the past "came" (आया), when after शायद it is the subjunctive.
notes: आए can also be the plural past; with शायद the subjunctive reading is the right one.

sentence: क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?
english: Can you help me?
harm: The learner is told सकते is a separate verb with its own meaning, when सकना only means "can" after a stem.

sentence: मैं यह सवाल हल नहीं कर पाया।
english: I could not manage to solve this question.
harm: The learner is told पाया means "found" or "got", when after a stem it means "managed to".

sentence: हमें बड़ों की बात माननी चाहिए।
english: We should obey our elders.
harm: The learner is not told that चाहिए with an infinitive means "should" and that माननी agrees with बात.

sentence: मैं अपने घर जाना चाहता हूँ।
english: I want to go to my home.
harm: The learner is told जाना चाहता हूँ is "I want" and a separate "to go" with no link, and misses that चाहना takes the infinitive.

sentence: वह लड़का स्कूल जा रहा है।
english: That boy is going to school.
harm: The learner is taught to say लड़का with three syllables (la-ra-ka), a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: The unwritten a after ड़ is not said; the word has two syllables, larka.

sentence: मुझे यह काम करना है।
english: I have to do this work.
harm: The learner is taught to say करना as ka-ra-na, a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: The a after र is not said.

sentence: मैं उसकी बात समझना चाहता हूँ।
english: I want to understand what he (or she) says.
harm: The learner is taught to say समझना as sa-ma-jha-na, a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: The first a is said, the one after झ is not.

sentence: तालाब में एक सफ़ेद कमल खिला है।
english: A white lotus has bloomed in the pond.
harm: The learner is taught to say कमल with a final a (kamala), a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: The final a is not said; the middle one is.

sentence: सरकार ने नया क़ानून बनाया।
english: The government made a new law.
harm: The learner is taught to say सरकार as sa-ra-kar, a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: The a after र is not said.

sentence: इस दवा का उपयोग सावधानी से करो।
english: Use this medicine with care.
harm: The learner is taught to say उपयोग with the middle a dropped (upyog), a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: The a after प is said (u-pa-yog); the word is not "upyog".

sentence: सब्ज़ी में थोड़ा नमक डालो।
english: Put a little salt in the vegetables.
harm: The learner is taught to say नमक with a final a (namaka), a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: The final a is not said, the middle one is.

sentence: उसने धीरे से दरवाज़ा खोला।
english: He (or she) opened the door slowly.
harm: The learner is taught to say दरवाज़ा as da-ra-va-za, a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: The a after र is not said: dar-vā-zā.

sentence: मेरा परिवार गाँव में रहता है।
english: My family lives in a village.
harm: The learner is taught to say परिवार with a wrong vowel in the first syllable, a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: All three syllables are said: pa-ri-vār.

sentence: दादी हमें रोज़ एक कहानी सुनाती हैं।
english: Grandmother tells us a story every day.
harm: The learner is taught to say कहानी as ka-ha-nī, a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: Spoken kahānī: the a after क is said, the one after ह is a long ā.

sentence: हमारे पास समय बहुत कम है।
english: We have very little time.
harm: The learner is taught to say समय with a dropped middle a (samy), a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: Both a's of समय are said; बहुत has two syllables.

sentence: वह बहुत भला आदमी है।
english: He is a very good man.
harm: The learner is taught to say आदमी as ā-da-mī, a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: The a after द is not said: ād-mī.

sentence: मुझे रोज़ सुबह पढ़ना अच्छा लगता है।
english: I like reading every morning.
harm: The learner is taught to say पढ़ना as pa-ṛha-na, a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: In पढ़ना the a after ढ़ is not said; in सुबह the a after ब is said (su-bah).

sentence: यह जवाब बिलकुल ठीक है।
english: This answer is perfectly right.
harm: The learner is taught to say जवाब with the wrong stress and vowels, a pronunciation no speaker uses.
notes: The transliteration writes व as v; spoken jawāb. The skeleton is only about where a is said.

sentence: मुझे ज़रा पानी दीजिए।
english: Please give me a little water.
harm: The learner is shown जरा, a different (Sanskrit) word meaning "old age", for the everyday "a little".
notes: I believe जरा (without nukta) exists as a separate word meaning "old age" and is rare; please confirm.

sentence: रोज़ सुबह हम टहलने जाते हैं।
english: We go for a walk every morning.
harm: The learner is shown रोज (without the dot), which is read and said as ज, not ज़.

sentence: मुझे हिंदी फ़िल्म देखना पसंद है।
english: I like watching Hindi films.
harm: The learner is shown फिल्म, which loses the f sound of the loan word.

sentence: यह कमरा बहुत साफ़ है।
english: This room is very clean.
harm: The learner is shown साफ, which changes how the last sound is said.

sentence: उसे हर चीज़ की जानकारी है।
english: He (or she) has information about everything.
harm: The learner is shown चीज, with the z sound lost.

sentence: ज़िंदगी में मेहनत बहुत ज़रूरी है।
english: Hard work is very necessary in life.
harm: The learner is shown जिंदगी and जरूरी, which lose the z sound.

sentence: बाज़ार से कुछ फल ले आओ।
english: Bring some fruit from the market.
harm: The learner is shown बाजार, which loses the z sound.

sentence: लड़की घर के बाहर खड़ी है।
english: The girl is standing outside the house.
harm: The learner is shown लडकी or खडी, with ड for ड़ (a different sound), and the word is not found.
notes: ड़ is a nukta letter too; खड़ा is an adjective/participle-like word, please say if you prefer VERB.

sentence: उसे माँ का प्रेम बहुत याद आता है।
english: He (or she) misses his mother's love very much.
harm: The learner is told प्रेम is not a word, because the conjunct प्र is not recognised.

sentence: विद्यार्थी कक्षा में चुपचाप बैठे हैं।
english: The students are sitting quietly in the classroom.
harm: The learner is shown a broken word, because द्य, र्थ or क्ष is not read as one unit.

sentence: उसे संस्कृत का बहुत ज्ञान है।
english: He (or she) has a lot of knowledge of Sanskrit.
harm: The learner is told ज्ञान is unknown, because ज्ञ is not recognised as a conjunct.

sentence: कृपया मुझे क्षमा कीजिए।
english: Please forgive me.
harm: The learner is told क्षमा is unknown and misses क्षमा करना as "to forgive".

sentence: रात को मैंने एक अजीब स्वप्न देखा।
english: In the night I saw a strange dream.
harm: The learner is told स्वप्न is not a word, because स्व and प्न are not read as conjuncts.

sentence: उसने अपना कर्तव्य ईमानदारी से निभाया।
english: He (or she) did his duty honestly.
harm: The learner is told कर्तव्य is unknown, because र्त and त्व are not read as one unit each.

sentence: इस विषय पर विद्वानों में मतभेद है।
english: Scholars disagree on this subject.
harm: The learner is not told that विषय is a learned, Sanskrit-derived word and takes it for an everyday one.

sentence: उसने अपनी ग़लती तुरंत मान ली।
english: He (or she) admitted his mistake at once.
harm: The learner is not told that ग़लती comes from the Perso-Arabic layer, as ज़रूरत and ज़िंदगी do.

sentence: मेरा फ़ोन कहीं खो गया है।
english: My phone has got lost somewhere.
harm: The learner is told फ़ोन is a native Hindi word and cannot see it is borrowed from English.

sentence: हम स्टेशन पर ट्रेन का इंतज़ार कर रहे हैं।
english: We are waiting for the train at the station.
harm: The learner is not told which words are English loans and which are Perso-Arabic, and takes all as one layer.

sentence: परमेश्वर सब पर दया करता है।
english: God shows mercy to all.
harm: The learner is not told that परमेश्वर is the word for God in the Hindi Bible and in church use, not in everyday speech.
notes: Sanskrit-derived and used in scripture; please say whether the register should be biblical, sanskritic or both.

sentence: प्रभु का अनुग्रह हम सब पर बना रहे।
english: May the grace of the Lord remain on us all.
harm: The learner is not told that अनुग्रह is the scriptural word for "grace" and not an everyday word.
notes: Unsure whether to tag this biblical or only sanskritic.

sentence: ज़रूरत पड़ने पर मुझे ज़रूर बुलाना।
english: When you need me, be sure to call me.
harm: The learner is not told that ज़रूरत is the Perso-Arabic everyday word whose formal partner is आवश्यकता.

sentence: आवश्यकता पड़ने पर मुझे अवश्य बुलाना।
english: When there is need, do call me without fail.
harm: The learner is not told that आवश्यकता is the formal Sanskrit-derived partner of ज़रूरत.

sentence: हम घर पर चाय पी रहे हैं।
english: We are drinking tea at home.
harm: The learner is told that plain words like घर and चाय are formal or foreign, and is not shown the everyday layer.

sentence: यह मेरी माँ की साड़ी है।
english: This is my mother's sari.
harm: The learner is told की is the verb "did", which makes the sentence meaningless.

sentence: उसने कल मुझसे बात की।
english: He (or she) spoke to me yesterday.
harm: The learner is told की means "of" and that "his talk of me" is meant, and misses बात करना.

sentence: किताब मेज़ पर रखी है।
english: The book is lying on the table.
harm: The learner is told पर means "but" and the sentence loses its place.

sentence: मैं उसके घर गया, पर वह नहीं मिला।
english: I went to his house, but I did not find him.
harm: The learner is told पर means "on" and cannot see the contrast between the two clauses.

sentence: राम और श्याम कल दिल्ली गए।
english: Ram and Shyam went to Delhi yesterday.
harm: The learner is told और means "more", and so Ram is "more Shyam".

sentence: कृपया मुझे और चावल दीजिए।
english: Please give me more rice.
harm: The learner is told और means "and" and that the sentence is incomplete.
notes: The meaning "more, another" before a noun is ADJ in some analyses, DET in others; the point is that it is not CCONJ. Please say which tag to require.

sentence: उसने सोने की अँगूठी पहनी।
english: She wore a gold ring.
harm: The learner is told सोने is a form of "to sleep" and that the ring is a "sleeping ring".

sentence: बच्चा रात को जल्दी सोना चाहता है।
english: The child wants to sleep early at night.
harm: The learner is told सोना is "gold" and that the child wants gold.

sentence: गर्मियों में आम बहुत मीठे होते हैं।
english: In summer mangoes are very sweet.
harm: The learner is told आम means "common" or "ordinary", and the sentence says nothing about fruit.

sentence: यहाँ यह आम बात है।
english: This is a common thing here.
harm: The learner is told आम is "mango" and that a mango thing is meant.

sentence: सरकार ने इस साल कर बढ़ा दिया।
english: The government raised the tax this year.
harm: The learner is told कर is the stem "do" (as in करके) and cannot make sense of the sentence.
notes: कर is "tax" (a noun) here; the stem कर of करना is the look-alike. Note बढ़ा दिया is also a compound.

sentence: तुम्हें समय पर खाना खाना चाहिए।
english: You should eat your meal on time.
harm: The learner is told both words are the same, so the sentence reads "meal meal" or "eat eat".

sentence: वह स्कूल गया। मैं घर पर रहा।
english: He went to school. I stayed at home.
harm: The learner is shown two sentences as one, and cannot tap a single sentence for its translation.

sentence: तुम कहाँ जा रहे हो? मैं भी चलूँगा।
english: Where are you going? I will come too.
harm: The learner is shown a question and its answer as one sentence.

sentence: उसने कहा, “मैं कल आऊँगा।” फिर वह चला गया।
english: He said, "I will come tomorrow." Then he left.
harm: The learner is shown the quotation cut at its danda and the closing quote starting a sentence of its own.
notes: The danda inside the quotation ends the sentence together with the closing quote mark; the next sentence starts with फिर.

sentence: डॉ. शर्मा कल दिल्ली जाएँगे।
english: Dr Sharma will go to Delhi tomorrow.
harm: The learner is shown "डॉ." as the end of a sentence, and the rest as a separate fragment.

sentence: क्या तुम आओगे? हाँ, मैं आऊँगा! ठीक है।
english: Will you come? Yes, I will come! All right.
harm: The learner is shown three short sentences as one block, or cut at the comma.

sentence: आज तापमान 32.5 डिग्री है।
english: Today the temperature is 32.5 degrees.
harm: The learner is shown the decimal point as a sentence end, and 32 and 5 in different sentences.

sentence: वह आया; मैं चला गया।
english: He came; I left.
harm: The learner is shown a semicolon as a sentence boundary and two fragments.
notes: Reviewer: for a reading app, should a semicolon count as a boundary? I assumed not.
